WHY IT WORKS

THE SCIENCE OF PRESENCE

01
SPATIAL MEMORY
Humans retain information 3–4× better when learned in 3D spatial context. The environment becomes part of the memory.
02
EMBODIMENT
Presence triggers genuine physiological and psychological responses. The brain treats virtual events as real.
03
SAFE FAILURE
High-risk procedures trained without consequence. Safety without exposure. Error as learning, not liability.

THE BROWSER / HEADSET CONNECTION

WHAT IS WEBXR?

WebXR is the browser API that connects an experience to an XR device. A session provides tracked views and input from supported controllers or hands. Three.js uses those views to render your scene for the headset.

ONE SCENE. DIFFERENT WAYS TO VIEW IT.

Three.js organizes meshes, materials, lights, and cameras.

WebGLRenderer draws that world.

WebXR supplies the headset session, tracked views, and XR input.

FROM A WEB PAGE TO IMMERSIVE VR

  1. Serve the app over HTTPS, or localhost during development.
  2. Check that the browser and device support an immersive session.
  3. The visitor chooses Enter VR and grants access.
  4. Render using the XR animation loop; respond to tracked input.
renderer.xr.enabled = true;
document.body.appendChild(VRButton.createButton(renderer));
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => {
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
});

A 3D canvas does not automatically enter VR. An AR session also needs browser and device support; a holographic-looking desktop scene is not camera-based AR.

SECTION 02

DESIGNING AN EXPERIENCE

01 COMFORT FIRST — NO MOTION SICKNESS
02 AFFORDANCES OVER INSTRUCTIONS
03 SPATIAL AUDIO GROUNDS PRESENCE
04 INTERACTION MUST FEEL PHYSICAL
05 LOCOMOTION DEFINES THE EXPERIENCE
06 PERFORMANCE IS A FEATURE — 72+ FPS

HOW USERS INTERACT

INTERACTION MODALITIES

01
GAZE
Eyes as pointer. Dwell-based activation. Always available — no peripheral required. Fatigue accumulates fast. Use for awareness, not precision.
LOW PRECISION / HANDS-FREE
02
CONTROLLER
6DOF tracked input. Trigger, grip, thumbstick, face buttons. Haptic feedback. The workhorse of VR. Precise, reliable, and universally understood.
HIGH PRECISION / HAPTICS
03
HAND TRACKING
No peripheral. Pinch to select, grab to manipulate. Feels natural — but occlusion, range limits, and latency demand careful affordance design.
NATURAL / CONTEXT-DEPENDENT
04
VOICE
Ambient, hands-free commands. Strong for navigation and mode switching. On-device models have latency. Not suitable as a primary interaction layer.
AMBIENT / SUPPLEMENTAL

DESIGN PATTERNS

INTERACTION PATTERNS

[ NEAR ]
DIRECT MANIPULATION
Reach into the world and grab. Intuitive because it mirrors physical reality. Requires spatial accuracy — arm fatigue is real above shoulder height.
RULE — Keep interactive objects within comfortable reach. No gorilla arm.
[ FAR ]
RAYCAST / POINTER
Project a ray from hand or gaze. Hover to target, trigger to select. The dominant pattern in most XR applications. Works at any distance.
RULE — Visual ray + cursor gives critical affordance feedback.
[ MOVE ]
LOCOMOTION
How users travel through virtual space. Teleport: safe, no sickness. Continuous: fast, disorienting for some. The choice shapes the entire experience feel.
RULE — Offer teleport as fallback. Comfort is non-negotiable.
[ UI ]
SPATIAL UI
UI lives in world space — not screen space. Panels, menus, labels anchored to the environment or to objects. Head-locked UI causes nausea. Do not do it.
RULE — No HUD. UI must exist in the world.

THE MENTAL MODEL

HOW THREE.JS WORKS

Three.js is a JavaScript library for building and rendering 3D scenes in the browser. Start with a small scene graph and add complexity one piece at a time.

SCENE → CAMERA → RENDERER

The scene holds your objects and lights. The camera chooses the viewpoint. The renderer draws what that camera can see.

GEOMETRY + MATERIAL = MESH

Geometry describes the shape. A material describes its surface. A mesh combines them and has a position, rotation, and scale.

const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(60, width / height, 0.1, 1000);
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer();
const cube = new THREE.Mesh(
  new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1),
  new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x00a8e8 })
);
scene.add(cube);
// Add lights, position the camera, then render each frame.

TRY IT IN THIS WORKSPACE

Build creates those meshes for you. The inspector edits transforms and materials. Play updates movement and physics, then the renderer draws the next frame. The WebXR examples below show the same progression in five stages.

Three.js fundamentals ↗

STAGE 01 / 05

AN EMPTY SCENE

— A renderer, a camera, a scene
— The foundation of every XR experience
— 72fps minimum. Non-negotiable.
const scene = new THREE.Scene()
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(
  75, w / h, 0.1, 1000
)
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer()
renderer.setAnimationLoop(render)

STAGE 02 / 05

GEOMETRY

— Objects: vertices, faces, UVs
— World space vs local space
— Transform: position, rotation, scale
const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1)
const mat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({
  wireframe: true
})
const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)
scene.add(mesh)

STAGE 03 / 05

LIGHTING + MATERIALS

— PBR materials respond to light
— Ambient + directional light setup
— Shadows cost — use with intention
const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
  color: 0x1b3d9e,
  roughness: 0.4,
  metalness: 0.6
})
const light = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1)
scene.add(light)

STAGE 04 / 05

INTERACTION

— Raycasting detects intersections
— Same pattern works with XR controllers
— Hover to highlight — click to activate
const ray = new THREE.Raycaster()
ray.setFromCamera(pointer, camera)
const hits = ray.intersectObjects(objects)
if (hits.length) {
  hits[0].object.material.emissive
    .set(0x00a8e8)
}

STAGE 05 / 05

AN EXPERIENCE

— Fog, particles, post-processing
— Environmental storytelling
— Every element earns its render cost
